faqs.question: What does AFB (TB) Antibiogram - Ofloxacin measure?
faqs.answer: This test measures the drug susceptibility of tuberculosis (TB) by analyzing the response to the antibiotic Ofloxacin.

faqs.question: Why is AFB (TB) Antibiogram - Ofloxacin done?
faqs.answer: • To know the drug susceptibility of tuberculosis (TB) • To guide doctors in selecting the most effective antibiotics for TB treatment • To prevent the development of drug-resistant TB • To monitor the effectiveness of TB treatment • To minimise the risk of TB transmission to others

faqs.question: When is AFB (TB) Antibiogram - Ofloxacin recommended and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: This test is recommended • for suspected or confirmed cases of tuberculosis, • when drug-resistant TB is suspected or present, • when monitoring the effectiveness of TB treatment, or • for individuals with symptoms such as persistent cough, weight loss, fatigue, and night sweats.

faqs.question: What if the results of the AFB (TB) Antibiogram - Ofloxacin are abnormal?
faqs.answer: Abnormal results indicate resistance to Ofloxacin, indicating a need for alternative medication options.

faqs.question: What to expect during the AFB (TB) Antibiogram - Ofloxacin?
faqs.answer: A healthcare professional will collect a TB bacteria specimen from your body. They will send the sample to the laboratory for analysis.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before the AFB (TB) Antibiogram - Ofloxacin?
faqs.answer: • Follow any specific instructions provided by your doctor or the laboratory. • Inform your doctor if you have any specific requirements.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with AFB (TB) Antibiogram - Ofloxacin?
faqs.answer: • GenXpert MTB/RIF: This test detects Mycobacterium tuberculosis DNA and checks its resistance to Rifampicin, another important anti-TB drug. • Acid-fast bacilli (AFB) smear: Microscopic examination of sputum or other samples to detect TB bacteria.

faqs.question: What is the AFB (TB) Antibiogram - Ofloxacin also known as?
faqs.answer: Tuberculosis Drug Susceptibility Test for Ofloxacin

faqs.question: What is Tuberculosis (TB)?
faqs.answer: Tuberculosis (TB) is a bacterial infection caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It primarily affects the lungs but can also involve other organs. TB is an airborne disease spread through respiratory droplets and commonly presents with symptoms like a persistent cough, fever, and weight loss.
